THE BRACKET. ELE rashe VET-avotam — 'THESE are the heads of their fathers' houses' (the bet of vet soft — MS's rafe ruling, asserted at the build): the narrative halts mid-commission and opens a REGISTRY (the letter's own order: before the speakers face Pharaoh, the book certifies who they are — the machine reads 6:14-25 as the credential-file the twin attestation-verses will sign); bene REUVEN be…

THE SECOND LINE. u-vene SHIMON — Simeon's six, closing on shaul ben- ha-KENAANIT ('the son of the CANAANITE woman' — the one annotated son in the two despatch-verses; the readings' hearings on Dinah's line named-only, unclaimed): the machine files the pattern — two tribal headers verbatim from Gen 46's ledger (the corpus's roster- file), and the list arrives at the tribe it came for.

THE THIRD LINE. ve-ELE SHEMOT bene LEVI — 'and these are the NAMES of the sons of Levi': the book of NAMES (shemot) re-sounds its title-word over the one tribe it will follow; li-TOLDOTAM — 'by their GENERATIONS' (the doubly-lean toledot-skeleton, gen_42's Vaera-pair file — this is that Vaera station); u-shene CHAYE LEVI — the registry starts counting LIFE-TOTALS (137; only Levi's line gets years …

THE FIRST HOUSE. bene GERSHON livni ve-shimi — Gershon's two, le- mishpechotam ('by their families'): the machine files the house- record plain (no etnachta in the five-word verse — the split rides the tifcha, the frame's own small pause).

THE COUSIN-LINE. u-vene YITZHAR: QORACH — the name enters the registry two generations before its rebellion (Num 16 armed at the entry itself; the machine files the record without foreknowledge — a name, a house, a family); ve-NEFEG ve-ZIKHRI close the verse (a three-name record, no etnachta-half needed beyond the header's pause).

THE CARRIER-LINE. u-vene UZIEL: MISHAEL ve-ELTZAFAN — the two cousins the corpus already needs: Lev 10:4 ('come near, carry your brothers from before the sanctuary') summons exactly these two names to carry Nadav and Avihu's bodies — and both the dead (6:23) and their bearers (here) enter the Torah in adjacent verses of one registry (the machine arms the cross-book receipt: the corpus's Leviticus …
